summary: Full backend + frontend E2E test of The Shopkeeper's Day PWA. Backend: 44/44 pytest cases pass across auth, khata (customers/entries/aging/cap/reminders), notifications, inventory (CRUD/low-stock/sales/stock-in), Gemini bill OCR, suppliers + PO lifecycle, analytics, and customer OTP portal (mocked Twilio), including auth-guard/403 role separation. Frontend: all 12 requested flows verified on desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844) — login, signup, khata add/credit/payment/aging, 1Cr hard block + 80L soft warning, MOCK reminder toast + bell notification, inventory add/edit/low-stock badge/cash sale/credit sale creating ledger entry, real Gemini OCR upload -> confirm -> stock-in (4/4 line items extracted correctly), supplier add + reorder suggestions + PO draft->sent->received (stock incremented), analytics charts with daily/weekly/monthly tabs + top items + aging pie, customer OTP portal with dev_otp toast and read-only khata, Hindi/English + dark/light toggles, and route guards. No blocking bugs found; issues are validation/security hardening and a data-integrity gap.

minor.issue: No file-type validation. Uploading a text/plain file ('notes.txt') returns 200 with hallucinated JSON instead of 400/415. Should whitelist image/png|jpeg|webp and cap file size.
No input validation: malformed email ('not-an-email') and 1-character password are accepted (200). Use pydantic EmailStr + min_length on password.
No brute-force protection — 7 consecutive wrong-password attempts all return 401 with no lockout/429 (auth playbook expects lockout after 5 fails).
Unlimited OTP verify attempts (12 wrong codes all just 401). A 6-digit OTP with no attempt cap / no per-phone send throttle is brute-forceable.

Orphan data: deleting a customer removes ledger_entries but NOT the sales docs created by credit entries/sales; deleted products stay in past sales. After deleting all test customers/products, /api/analytics/summary still reports today_sales=8007540 with 8 txns for non-existent customers, inflating dashboard + analytics.
allow_credentials=True combined with allow_origins=['*'] is an invalid/ignored combination per the CORS spec; set explicit origins from env.

issues: Y-axis tick label clipped — '₹1,00,00,000' renders as ',00,00,000' (increase YAxis width/left margin)
With a single bucket the bar spans nearly the whole chart width, looking like a filled block
Recharts console warning: 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' fires on chart mount (container has no minWidth/minHeight)
Empty state renders an axis-only chart with no 'no data' message
'TODAY'S SALES: ₹0' label wraps to two lines and collides visually with the period tabs
Qty and unit-price inputs have no column headers/labels — user can't tell which numeric column is qty vs price
Credit-sale note shows float qty: 'Sale: QA Prod 846 x1.0' instead of 'x1'

action_items: Validate OCR upload content_type (image/png|jpeg|webp) + max size; reject others with 400/415.
Add EmailStr + password min_length (>=6) validation to /api/auth/register.
Add login rate-limit/lockout after 5 failed attempts and cap OTP verify attempts (e.g. 5) + throttle OTP sends per phone.
Cascade-clean sales/purchase-order references when a customer or product is deleted (or filter analytics to existing customers) so dashboard/analytics totals stay accurate.
Set explicit CORS origins from env instead of '*' while allow_credentials=True.
Analytics chart polish: YAxis width for ₹1Cr labels, min height/width on ResponsiveContainer to silence recharts warning, empty-data message.
Format qty as integer when whole number in ledger note and OCR confirm rows; add qty/price column headers on the OCR confirm table.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /api/inventory/ocr trusts file.content_type for both the temp-file suffix and the Gemini mime type — an attacker-supplied mime lets arbitrary non-image bytes reach the LLM; validate against an allowlist and sniff the magic bytes.

server.py: aging/list endpoints call compute_aging per customer with a per-customer ledger query (N+1). Fine for MVP scale but will degrade with a few thousand customers — aggregate with a single $group query.
server.py: all list endpoints use fixed .to_list(2000/5000) with no pagination; add limit/skip params before data grows.
server.py: create_entry inserts a sales doc for every khata credit entry, so 'today's sales' counts pure ledger credits; document/intend this, and make deletion consistent.
Tests live under /app/backend/tests, which triggers uvicorn WatchFiles reloads on edit — harmless but consider excluding the tests dir from the reload watch.

success_rate.backend: 100% (44/44 functional); 0/5 hardening probes in test_edge_cases.py pass

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable suites: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (44 functional tests, run with `pytest -n 0 -p no:randomly` because classes share state), /app/backend/tests/test_edge_cases.py (5 hardening probes, all currently failing by design — re-run after validation/rate-limit fixes), /app/backend/tests/make_bill.py (synthetic bill PNG generator for OCR). For UI OCR testing, build the bill image in-browser via canvas.toDataURL and pass the decoded bytes to set_input_files(buffer=...). Sell dialog mode options are labelled 'Cash Sale' / 'Credit Sale'. Gemini OCR responded in ~10-20s and extracted 4/4 line items accurately.
rca_of_the_issue: Analytics inflation RCA: POST /api/khata/entries inserts a db.sales doc for every credit entry, but DELETE /api/khata/customers only removes db.customers + db.ledger_entries. Sales rows therefore survive customer deletion and are still summed by /api/analytics/summary and /api/analytics/sales (which filter only by owner_id + date), leaving today_sales=₹80,07,540 for customers that no longer exist. Fix: delete/soft-flag sales on customer delete, or join sales against existing customers in analytics.
